paper_title: Bootstrap for finite N lattice Yang-Mills theory (Kazakov, 2025, JHEP)
deeper_reasoning_1:
\section*{Claim}
Let $G\in\{U(N),SU(N)\}$ with finite $N\ge2$. Define the retained trace bound
\[
b_G:=\begin{cases}
N,&G=U(N),\\
N-1,&G=SU(N).
\end{cases}
\]
If every unreduced loop variation of a retained Wilson-loop monomial produces terms with at most $b_G+1$ normalized trace factors, and if the finite-$N$ trace identities define a linear reduction map
\[
R_{G,N}:\mathcal T_{b_G+1}\longrightarrow \mathcal T_{b_G},
\]
then the trace-reduced loop-equation system closes on the retained variables in $\mathcal T_{b_G}$.
\section*{Premises}
\[
\begin{aligned}
\text{(P1)}&\quad \mathcal T_m:=\operatorname{span}\{\text{Wilson-loop monomials with at most }m\text{ trace factors}\}.\\
\text{(P2)}&\quad E_{\rm var}:\mathcal T_{b_G}\to\mathcal T_{b_G+1}\text{ is the unreduced Schwinger--Dyson or Makeenko--Migdal variation}.\\
\text{(P3)}&\quad R_{G,N}:\mathcal T_{b_G+1}\to\mathcal T_{b_G}\text{ is linear and equals the identity on }\mathcal T_{b_G}.\\
\text{(P4)}&\quad \text{The exact finite-}N\text{ trace identities are valid under the same Haar integral}.\\
\text{(P5)}&\quad E_{\rm loop}:=R_{G,N}\circ E_{\rm var}.
\end{aligned}
\]
\section*{Derivation}
Take any retained monomial $X\in\mathcal T_{b_G}$. By (P2),
\[
E_{\rm var}(X)\in\mathcal T_{b_G+1}.
\]
Applying the finite-$N$ reduction gives
\begin{align}
E_{\rm loop}(X)
&=(R_{G,N}\circ E_{\rm var})(X) &&\text{by (P5)}\\
&=R_{G,N}(E_{\rm var}(X)) &&\text{definition of composition}\\
&\in R_{G,N}(\mathcal T_{b_G+1}) &&\text{because }E_{\rm var}(X)\in\mathcal T_{b_G+1}\\
&\subseteq \mathcal T_{b_G} &&\text{by (P3)}.
\end{align}
Thus every generated equation can be expressed using only variables with at most $b_G$ trace factors. Since (P4) states that the reduction identities are exact inside the same integral, this substitution changes the representation of the equation but not its projected Wilson-loop solution set.
\section*{Final Result}
\[
\boxed{E_{\rm loop}(\mathcal T_{b_G})\subseteq\mathcal T_{b_G},\qquad b_{U(N)}=N,
\qquad b_{SU(N)}=N-1.}
\]
\hfill$\blacksquare$

deeper_reasoning_4:
\section*{Claim}
Let the $SU(2)$ hierarchy-truncated plaquette feasible set be
\[
\mathcal F_{\Lambda,d,\lambda}:=\{w\in\mathbb R^q: A_{\Lambda,d,\lambda}w=b_{\Lambda,d,\lambda}\text{ and }M_{r,\Lambda,d,\lambda}(w)\succeq0\text{ for all retained }r\},
\]
where the retained loop length satisfies $L_{\max}=8\Lambda$. If the exact projected Wilson-loop vector $w^*$ lies in $\mathcal F_{\Lambda,d,\lambda}$ and $u_P(w)=c_P^Tw$, then the endpoints
\[
L_{\Lambda,d,\lambda}(u_P):=\min_{w\in\mathcal F_{\Lambda,d,\lambda}}c_P^Tw,
\qquad
U_{\Lambda,d,\lambda}(u_P):=\max_{w\in\mathcal F_{\Lambda,d,\lambda}}c_P^Tw
\]
certify the plaquette interval.
\section*{Premises}
\[
\begin{aligned}
\text{(P1)}&\quad d\in\{2,3,4\},\quad \Lambda\in\mathbb Z_{\ge0},\quad \lambda>0,\quad L_{\max}=8\Lambda.\\
\text{(P2)}&\quad A_{\Lambda,d,\lambda}w=b_{\Lambda,d,\lambda}\text{ is the retained linear }SU(2)\text{ loop-equation system}.\\
\text{(P3)}&\quad M_{r,\Lambda,d,\lambda}(w)=M_{r,0}+\sum_j w_jM_{r,j}\succeq0\text{ are retained Hermitian or reflection positivity blocks}.\\
\text{(P4)}&\quad w^*\in\mathcal F_{\Lambda,d,\lambda}.\\
\text{(P5)}&\quad u_P(w^*)=c_P^Tw^*\text{ is the exact projected plaquette average}.\\
\text{(P6)}&\quad L_{\Lambda,d,\lambda}(u_P)\text{ and }U_{\Lambda,d,\lambda}(u_P)\text{ are computed over the same feasible set}.
\end{aligned}
\]
\section*{Derivation}
Since $w^*\in\mathcal F_{\Lambda,d,\lambda}$ by (P4), the definition of a minimum gives
\begin{align}
L_{\Lambda,d,\lambda}(u_P)
&=\min_{w\in\mathcal F_{\Lambda,d,\lambda}}c_P^Tw\\
&\le c_P^Tw^*.
\end{align}
Similarly, the definition of a maximum gives
\begin{align}
c_P^Tw^*&\le \max_{w\in\mathcal F_{\Lambda,d,\lambda}}c_P^Tw
=U_{\Lambda,d,\lambda}(u_P).
\end{align}
Using (P5), these inequalities become
\begin{align}
L_{\Lambda,d,\lambda}(u_P)&\le u_P(w^*)\le U_{\Lambda,d,\lambda}(u_P).
\end{align}
Because both endpoints use the same feasible set by (P6), the interval is a certified consequence of feasibility, not a comparison between different relaxations. The role of $L_{\max}=8\Lambda$ in (P1) is to specify exactly which loop variables and positivity blocks are included in that same finite relaxation.
\section*{Final Result}
\[
\boxed{u_P(w^*)\in\left[L_{\Lambda,d,\lambda}(u_P),U_{\Lambda,d,\lambda}(u_P)\right]\quad\text{for each retained }(\Lambda,d,\lambda).}
\]
\hfill$\blacksquare$
